JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioners in the nutshell:

It is the case of the petitioner that on 19.07.2023 at about 1.00 p.m, the SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 deceased in order to draw money in the Bank was going to Fedral Bank, J.P.Nagar Branch and while crossing the road, the respondent No.1 being the driver of the vehicle owned by the respondent No.2 drove the car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MH-3683 with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life, lost control over his vehicle and dashed to the deceased and caused the accident.
As a result of impact deceased fell on the road and sustained fatal injuries all over the body and succumbed to the fatal injuries.
Post mortem was conducted and body of the deceased handed over to the petitioner.
It is further contended that for funeral and obsequies ceremonies the petitioner has spent substantial amount.
It is further urged that because of untimely death of deceased, the petitioner has suffered economically as well as emotionally.

It is specifically urged that the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the car driver and as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation with interest and cost.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
Notice was duly served to respondent No.1 & 2.

Respondent No.1 & 2 appeared through their counsel by filing common written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondents denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
Per contra contended that the accident occurred purely on the negligence on the part of deceased herself.
It is contended that the respondent No.1 was driving the car belonging to the respondent No.2.
Further the respondent No.2 is the owner of the car and respondent No.1 is having valid DL and the said vehicle on the date of accident.
Further the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MH-3683 was duly insured with the 3rd respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. The respondent No.3 entered appearance and filed written statement denying the petition averments.

sentences.text: This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident.
Further contended that the insured vehicle is falsely implicated in the alleged accident.
Further negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied.
Per contra it is alleged that the unfortunate accident occurred on account of the sole negligence of the deceased without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.

Further it is contended that the petitioner is major son, according to the petition they are legal heir of deceased and he was not the dependent of deceased, hence he is not entitled to any compensation as the dependency of the SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 deceased.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he is the legal heir and dependent of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19.07.2023 at about 1.00 p.m.,
Opposite Shell Petrol Bunk, Ring road 15th Cross, J.P.Nagara 6th Phase, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence of the driver of the Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-MH-3683 ?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed ?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?

sentences.text: From the evidence on record it is seen that after the receipt of complaint lodged by son of the petitioner, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MH-3683 for the offences punishable u/s's 279 & 304(A) of IPC and u/s 56, 192 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
In order to disprove the defence, the respondent No.1 being the driver of offending car himself was examined as RW.1.
RW.1 in his chief examination he reiterated the written statement averments.
During the course of his cross examination RW.1 admitted that the offending vehicle was standing in the name of his brother.
He admitted that as on the date and time of accident he was driving the car and also admitted the cause of accident.
He admitted that after the accident he accompanied the injured and shifted to the hospital and during the course of treatment she died.
Further it is categorically admitted by RW.1 during the course of cross examination that Police filed FIR against him and also filed charge sheet against him and his brother.
Further he denied the negligence on his part but stated that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased.
This categorical admission also adds to the case of the petitioner.
Thus the unchallenged charge sheet clearly establishes negligence on the part of driver of car.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MH-3683.
As such, I answer Issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.1:
The petitioner claim that he is the son of the deceased.

To prove the same,
petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of his chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioner with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Further the respondent No.3 contended that the petitioner is major son, according to the petition he is legal heir of deceased and he is not the dependent of deceased, hence he is not entitled to any compensation as the dependency of the deceased.
12.
At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2021 SCC Online Kerala 3209 (United India Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Shalumol and Others).

sentences.text:
In a recent decision in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356], a claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother, the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited v.
Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meager income between Rs. 1,00,000/and Rs.
1,50,000/per annum.
In that sense, they were largely dependent on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years."

Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala and Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the major married / earning sons and married daughters are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor vehicles accident cases.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners, with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioner is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 Tribunal hold that the petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner is the legal heir and dependent of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.3 :
So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, petitioner has not produced any documents to show the age of the deceased.
Hence the age of the deceased as indicated in the police and medical records i.e., 44 years is taken into consideration.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '14'.
14.
In this case the petitioner has claimed the compensation on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.

sentences.text: To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioner has produced the appointment letter at Ex.P.12.
Except Ex.P12 he has not produced any other documents or examined the author to prove the income of the deceased.
Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2023.
It is trite law that, when the petitioner has failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

15. As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 25%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 44 years.
Therefore, in this case, 25% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 44 years SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 and as such, 25% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.20,000/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/- + 4,000/- i.e. 25%).
16.
The deceased died living behind one dependent.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/2 of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.10,000/- p.m. (Rs.20,000 - Rs.10,000 = Rs.10,000/-).
17. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,000/- p.m. and the multiplier '14' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.16,80,000/- (Rs.10,000/- X 12 X 14).

21. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
22. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of Insurance Policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
The Insurance Company only contended that its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It was submitted that the owner of the car had violated the terms and conditions of the policy as the said vehicle was plied without FC.

sentences.text: Even otherwise absence of Fitness SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 certificate cannot be a ground to exonerate the Insurance Company from payment of compensation.
The deceased is a 3rd party to the above car.
The third parties rights are very well protected under M.V.Act.
The lapse of Fitness Certificate would not constitute breach of provisions of MV Act.
In the absence of FC cannot be ground to exonerate the insurance company.
In this regard it is relevant to relied on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in 2020 ACJ 489 (KAR) in case of Rajesh Poojary V/s Rajesh and another.

entities.text: Rajesh Poojary V/s Rajesh and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that :
"9.

The Division bench of this Court in a decision rendered in the case of New India Assurance Co.Ltd v. N. Srinivasa Murthy, MFA No.6621/2006 c/w MFA CROB.No.304/2006; decided on 18.09.2007, has observed that 'absence of fitness certificate cannot be a reason to deny the compensation to the claimant'.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co.Ltd v. N. Srinivasa Murthy, MFA No.6621/2006 c/w MFA CROB.No.304/2006;
entities.label: PRECEDENT

A coordinate Bench of this court in the case of Branch Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd., v. H.D. Channadevaiah, MFA.No.4428/2013 c/w MFA.No.3553/2013 ;
decided on 25.06.2017, held in a similar circumstance, where the insured vehicle did not possess fitness certificate as on the date of accident, that SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 'the policy was in force on the date of accident and the insurance company cannot disown its liability".

entities.text: Branch Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd., v. H.D. Channadevaiah, MFA.No.4428/2013 c/w MFA.No.3553/2013 ;
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. The Tribunal while fixing the liability on the insured placed reliance on the decision of Kerala High Court in the case of Tharva v. Syamala, 2009 ACJ 2440 (Kerala).
It is pertinent to note that the said decision of Kerala High Court has been overruled by the Full Bench decision in the case of Augustine V.M. v. Ayyappankutty, 2015 ACJ 2142 (Kerala).
It is held that lapse of certificate of fitness would constitute breach of provisions of Motor Vehicles Act or Rules.
However, there is nothing under section 56 of the Act, which suggests that the registration or permit issued would stand cancelled or revoked on account of lapse of period of fitness certificate".
On the above said judgment relying on the various decisions had laid down absence of Fitness certificate cannot be a reason to deny the compensation to the claimant.
It is also held that the policy was in force on the date of accident, the insurance company cannot be disown its liability.
It is further forthcoming from the above said decision that the lapse of certificate of fitness would constitute breach of the provisions of Motor SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 Vehicles Act or Rules.

As such the respondent No.3 insurance company is liable to pay compensation.
23.
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the driver and owner of offending car and respondent No.3 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
As a result of impact deceased fell on the road and sustained fatal injuries all over the body and succumbed to the fatal injuries.
It is contended that the respondent No.1 was driving the car belonging to the respondent No.2.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that he is the legal heir and dependent of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19.07.2023 at about 1.00 p.m.,
Opposite Shell Petrol Bunk, Ring road 15th Cross, J.P.Nagara 6th Phase, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence of the driver of the Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-MH-3683 ?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed ?
If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
From the evidence on record it is seen that after the receipt of complaint lodged by son of the petitioner, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the Innova car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-MH-3683 for the offences punishable u/s's 279 & 304(A) of IPC and u/s 56, 192 of IMV Act.
Since the evidence led by the petitioner is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 Tribunal hold that the petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner is the legal heir and dependent of deceased.
So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, petitioner has not produced any documents to show the age of the deceased.
Hence the age of the deceased as indicated in the police and medical records i.e., 44 years is taken into consideration.
In this case the petitioner has claimed the compensation on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
It is trite law that, when the petitioner has failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
15. As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 44 years.
Therefore, in this case, 25% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.
19. In this case, the petitioner is the son of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018)
12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner is entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and parents as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a mother cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her mother.
The Insurance Company only contended that its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The deceased is a 3rd party to the above car.
The third parties rights are very well protected under M.V.Act.
The lapse of Fitness Certificate would not constitute breach of provisions of MV Act.
In the absence of FC cannot be ground to exonerate the insurance company.
A coordinate Bench of this court in the case of Branch Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd., v. H.D. Channadevaiah, MFA.No.4428/2013 c/w MFA.No.3553/2013 ;
decided on 25.06.2017, held in a similar circumstance, where the insured vehicle did not possess fitness certificate as on the date of accident, that SCCH-23 MVC.4067/2024 'the policy was in force on the date of accident and the insurance company cannot disown its liability".
There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Further the respondent No.3 contended that the petitioner is major son, according to the petition he is legal heir of deceased and he is not the dependent of deceased, hence he is not entitled to any compensation as the dependency of the deceased.
12.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under the head of Filial consortium.
opennyai_summary.decision:
17. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,000/- p.m. and the multiplier '14' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.16,80,000/- (Rs.10,000/- X 12 X 14).
As such the respondent No.3 insurance company is liable to pay compensation.
23.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the driver and owner of offending car and respondent No.3 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However, the respondent No.3 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Accordingly issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.17,56,300/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.3 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
